findings.quote: Recalling a nearby but incorrect value from the same curve gives 0.6 fm instead of 0.8 fm.
findings.note: This entry is circular: it says that recalling an incorrect value produces the incorrect value. It gives the student no way to tell 0.6 fm from 0.8 fm, so it is a generic warning rather than a named error route on this question.
findings.fix: 0.6 fm is still inside the repulsive part of the curve, where the potential energy is rising, not at the minimum; the minimum is at about 0.8 fm.

notes: Solved independently before reading the solution: the nucleon-nucleon potential energy curve is strongly repulsive below about 0.8 fm and attractive beyond it, with the minimum at r0 = 0.8 fm (the value quoted in the Class 12 nuclei chapter). Option 3. The steps and common_mistakes[0] are correct as written. difficulty 'medium' for a pure recall item is on the high side but not clearly off, so not filed.
